title: A Black Hole Is Humming a Note 57 Octaves Too Deep to Hear

scenes.text: A black hole is humming. We just can't hear it.
In the Perseus galaxy cluster, 250 million light-years away, NASA's Chandra telescope spotted ripples in hot gas.
The ripples are about 30,000 light-years apart. Scientists read them as sound waves.
Outbursts from the supermassive black hole push the gas aside and send the waves out.
The note is a B flat, 57 octaves below middle C. Far deeper than any ear can hear.
The loudest thing in that cluster is a black hole. You'll never hear it.

description:
A black hole is humming a note, and we can never hear it.
NASA's Chandra X-ray telescope found ripples in the hot gas of the Perseus cluster, 250 million light-years away. Read as sound waves, they make a B flat 57 octaves below middle C.
What do you think a black hole would sound like?
first_comment: If a black hole could sing, what song would it pick?
